memos.risk:
Risk view: this is a weak setup, so I'd refuse, not size it.

Red flags: 100% bundle share on the curve, a launch bot present, top-5 buyers holding 56% of early buys, and sell-to-buy of 0.54 right after graduation. Drawdown is already 33% off the 30-minute high, and the last 15 minutes show heavy distribution (1,685 SOL sold vs 1,799 bought, 888 sellers). The 0.6 completer share and 53% top-3 concentration point to insiders taking the early supply. The name "Unites States" is a generic, possibly borrowed label and is not a signal.

Pool depth of ~232 SOL and $412K in 15-minute volume are adequate for a $20 ticket, so liquidity isn't the constraint. Concentration and distribution are.

If the desk insists on buying anyway, the most conservative terms would be a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But I'd refuse at any size: the bundling, launch bot, and active selling make this closer to a trap than an organic run, and skipping costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping.

What supports demand: the last 15 minutes show real turnover ($412k volume, 767 buyers, a 1.28x return) and the coin is still above its 30-minute-ago level (+111%). Post-graduation buyers ex-agent are 59, and the pool holds 232 SOL.

What undercuts it: the curve was 100% bundled with 60% taken by the completer, and the top 3 buyers hold 53%. Post-graduation, sells are 54% of buys and the top 5 buyers account for 56% of flow. Net flow over 15 minutes is only +113 SOL against 1,685 SOL sold, and the coin has already fallen 33% from its 30-minute high. A launch bot was present. Sellers (888) outnumber buyers (767) in the last window. That pattern looks like early holders distributing into fresh demand, not demand that will hold 30-60 minutes out.

No clear case for buying now. The volume is real, but it is concentrated, distribution-heavy, and already off its high. Given fees of 1.4-5.1% and a base rate near -20% for this profile, I'd pass.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution after a 128% run. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 with the completer holding 60% and the top 3 wallets at 53%, so a few insiders control the float. Last 15 minutes show $412k volume, with 1,685 SOL sold against 1,799 bought and 888 sellers, so sell pressure is already heavy. The price is down 33% from its 30-minute high, and the first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.54 with a launch bot present and the top 5 buyers taking 56%. A 33% drawdown on a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leaves little room for a bounce to pay off. Skip.
